correctness.rationale: For \(q=799/800\), the site failure function is \(f(z)=[1+799(1+z)e^{-z}]/800\), and total failure is \(F(x)=f(x)f(10-x)\) globally for \(0\le x\le10\). The exact logarithmic derivative sign reduces to that of \(799-G(5-x)\), where \(G(u)=e^5[5\sinh(u)/u-\cosh(u)]\). The proven power-series identity for the auxiliary function \(J(u)/u^3\) is strictly decreasing, so \(G\) has one maximum. Exact rational intervals certify two and only two crossings, in \(u\in(2,3)\) and \(u\in(4,5)\); \(F(3)<F(0),F(5)\) excludes concentration and equality. Reflection yields exactly two global minima, and derivative transversality plus strict separation proves robustness. The checker certifies rational signs; finite numerical sampling is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural stochastic bottleneck—two arrivals required for local viability combined with independent site suitability—can defeat both concentrating effort and splitting it equally even between identical habitats. The proof establishes a genuinely robust symmetry-breaking optimum, so a common endpoint-or-equal allocation shortlist is incomplete for expected-effort introductions. The exact result motivates careful release-allocation calculations without claiming field predictive performance; it is not merely a numerical lookup or arbitrary unmotivated slice.
